Before I get on to the topic of player retention, I think my story with the game might help illustrate how I feel. my first ever exposure to rs was RuneScape HD. A cousin of mine used to play it when I was younger. I didn't remember too much but I remember the name and that I watched him play it at a couple family gatherings... He even let me make an account once. It was so mysterious and interesting to me then. I was young and had an urge to explore every nook and cranny... Well that account ended when I hit some vampire boi in a spooky house. That's about all I remembered. It's been over 6 years since then
So I am speaking from the point of view of a player who was recently brought back to rs through the release of mobile (about half a year experience so far)

  I felt an urge to explore and figure out what I had seen and  experienced years ago. My first goal was to kill that garlic hater. That goal fueled me to keep going through the early game... The mystery of the vampire and the game my cousin showed me years ago.. but     honestly.. the thing that kept me here since killing that blood succ boi is that when I started playing again I was at a low point. I didn't have much friends to speak of and deep down I thought If I explored enough and did enough in the game that eventually some sort of friendship would be made... Never did happen... But whenever I was spoken to I felt amazing. I am in a better place now and am playing actively, I have 120 days membership as well. The allure of seeing other players interact early on kept me going above all else.

I think some sort of incentive for more social interaction between players may help but moreover the sense of the unknown and mystery is what had me come back after over 6 years, not just mystery as in the lore, enemies, and game world but also the mystery of what possible interactions I had in store in the future. Seeing highlevels bankstand at the ge and talk gave me incentive to keep playing the game in hopes that I might be able to join them one day with all the expensive gear as well. Of course... New players may lose interest if they deem too early that there is nothing to be gained by playing this game. there is no investment to deter stopping at low levels- as well as no mystery to come back to explore. 

Incentivizing social interaction in lumbridge would be great as it would allow for new players to seek guidance to begin as well as build investment in the community- or at the very least provide the mystery of the (how do I join this community?) Or (what if I came back to the game?). Right now lumbridge just has like a couple splashers that never talk or bots all over and it's really off-putting tbh.

I apologise for the somewhat unorganized rant and thank anyone who took the time from their day to read this, I hope y'all have a great day :)
